The factory is the very big room on the far side of the site. Next to it is  $ \underline{\text{the warehouse, which}} $ Q16 can be accessed by lorries going up the road to the turning area at the end. You can get to the warehouse by crossing to the far side of the courtyard, and then the door is on your right.

Somewhere you'll be keen to find is  $ \underline{\text{the staff canteen. This is right next to reception}} $. I can confidently say that the food's very good, but the view isn't.  $ \underline{\text{The windows on one side look onto a corridor and courtyard}} $, which aren't very attractive at all,  $ \underline{\text{and on the other onto the access road}} $, which isn't much better.

You'll be using  $ \underline{\text{the meeting room}} $ quite often, and you'll find it by walking along the corridor to the left of the courtyard, and continuing along it to the end. The meeting room is the last one on the right, and I'm afraid there's no natural daylight in the room.

Then you'll need to know where some of the offices are.  $ \underline{\text{The human resources department is at the front of this building, so you head to the left along the corridor from reception, and it's the second room you come to. It looks out onto the main road.}} $ Q19

And finally,  $ \underline{\text{the boardroom}} $, where you'll be meeting sometimes. That has quite a pleasant view, as it  $ \underline{\text{looks out on to the trees}} $. Go along the corridor past the courtyard, right to the end.  $ \underline{\text{The boardroom is on the left, next to the factory.}} $
OK, now are there any questions before we ...
PART 3
JESS: How are you getting on with your art project, Tom?

TOM: OK. Like, they gave us the theme of birds to base our project on, and I'm not really all that interested in wildlife. But I'm starting to get into it. I've pretty well finished the introductory stage.

JESS: So have I. When they gave us  $ \underline{\text{all those handouts with details of books and websites to look at}} $, I was really put off, but  $ \underline{\text{the more I read, the more interested I got}} $.
TOM:  $ \underline{\text{Me too. I found I could research so many different aspects of birds in art – colour, movement, texture.}} $ So I was looking forward to the Bird Park visit.

JESS: What a letdown! It poured with rain and we hardly saw a single bird.  $ \underline{\text{Much less}} $ Q21/Q22
 $ \underline{\text{use than the trip to the Natural History Museum.}} $
TOM:  $ \underline{\text{Yeah. I liked all the stuff about evolution there.}} $ The workshop sessions with Dr Fletcher were good too, especially the brainstorming sessions.
JESS: I missed those because I was ill. I wish we could've seen the projects last year's students did.
TOM: Mm. I suppose they want us to do our own thing, not copy.
JESS: Have you drafted your proposal yet?

TOM: Yes, but I haven't handed it in. I need to amend some parts. I've realised the notes from my research are almost all just descriptions, I haven't actually evaluated anything. So I'll have to fix that. Q23/Q24

JESS: Oh, I didn't know we had to do that.  $ \underline{\text{I'll have to look at that too.}} $ Did you do a timeline for the project?
TOM: Yes, and a mind man
TOM: Yes, and a mind map.
JESS: Yeah, so did I. I quite enjoyed that. But it was hard having to explain the basis for my decisions in my action plan.
